title: Power Automate: Delinea Secret Server as a credential provider for desktop flows
summary: The roadmap facts and both existing UI paths check out, but Microsoft documents credential creation and access-management APIs that the briefing reports as absent. The rollout advice also assumes an undocumented Delinea service account, machine-to-vault connectivity and sharing model, and overstates what credential sharing controls.

claims.claim: Teams with machine accounts in Delinea would otherwise have to copy passwords to Azure Key Vault or CyberArk or type them into desktop flow connections.

claims.fix: Replace the necessity claim with: 'A native provider could reduce the need to duplicate or manually maintain credentials in existing desktop flow configurations.' Keep this explicitly as the wiki's expectation, not an exhaustive statement of current integration options.

claims.where: Why it matters: second paragraph; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The planned Delinea provider will use a Delinea-side service account.
claims.quote: Searched: "Delinea" Power Automate desktop credential authentication machine network service account. Opened both existing provider pages and Secret Server (Preview); its application account belongs to the separate connector. Roadmap specifies no authentication identity.
claims.fix: Replace 'who owns the Delinea-side service account that Power Automate will use' with 'who will own the authentication identity, if one is required'. Make the service-account and folder-permission checklist conditional on Microsoft's eventual provider authentication documentation.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: indirect costs; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The Delinea provider requires the machines running desktop flows to reach the Delinea Secret Server instance directly.
claims.quote: Searched: "Delinea" Power Automate desktop credential authentication machine network service account. Opened both existing provider pages and Secret Server (Preview); only CyberArk documents machine-to-vault connectivity, not the planned Delinea architecture.
claims.fix: Replace the asserted machine connectivity requirement with 'Confirm Microsoft's documented network requirements and which component contacts Delinea before changing firewall rules.' Describe infrastructure costs as possible rather than a verified machine-to-vault prerequisite.

claims.claim: The Delinea-held account's permissions, not Power Automate, bound what the flow can do.
claims.quote: When a desktop flow is triggered by a cloud flow, the actions contained in the desktop flow that require elevated privileges won't have any effect. Therefore, Power Automate won't be able to access applications that run with elevated rights.
claims.fix: Remove 'not Power Automate'. Say 'Review the account's permissions as one security boundary; Power Automate execution restrictions and other applicable controls also constrain the flow.' Cite this page if explaining the elevated-rights restriction.
